found_values.value: No finite longest stall with the firmware as written; 900 ms for one main-loop pass in which the USB host stops reading. (a) One flash window a pass: out_store_tick() runs once a pass, and out_store_reclaim() only on a pass where the tick returned OUT_STORE_IDLE (main.c:1049, :1083); the longest window is one 4 kB sector erase, 400 ms maximum (packaged-part figure, W25Q16JV-DTR revision I tSE; the die's figure is not known). (b) Each console printf after it (main.c:1059-1067, :1084) blocks in pico-sdk 2.3.0 stdio_usb_out_chars(), which leaves its loop only when no space is free and more than PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US has passed since the last accepted chunk (stdio_usb.c:122); last_avail_time is reset at each accepted chunk (stdio_usb.c:118); the default is 500,000 us (stdio_usb.h:31-33) and no file under firmware/ or shared/ overrides it. (c) 400 ms erase plus one 500 ms blocked write: 900 ms. (d) With a host that keeps accepting slowly, each accepted chunk restarts the 500 ms, so the stall has no bound but the message length. (e) At boot, up to OUT_STORE_SECTORS = 2 erases (main.c:937-942, out_store.h:122) before can_start(): 800 ms plus prints, counted only if the watchdog runs by then. Q8 moves the output binding to an I2C FRAM (owner, 2026-09-29), which removes the erase once the firmware follows it; the firmware in this checkout still erases flash

report.value: The RP2350 watchdog counts down in microseconds from LOAD (24 bits, up to 0xffffff, 'approximately 16 seconds', Table 1249), is disabled at reset (CTRL.ENABLE 0x0) and pauses in debug (PAUSE_DBG0, PAUSE_DBG1, PAUSE_JTAG reset 1, Table 1248). Against the stop deadline (V1, 500 ms): the part can set any timeout under 500 ms; the time from expiry to the pads at their reset state is not stated. Against the longest legitimate stall (V2 as found): 900 ms for a pass with a 400 ms packaged-part sector erase and one 500 ms blocked console write, and no bound with a host that keeps accepting slowly, since each accepted chunk restarts pico-sdk 2.3.0's 500,000 us PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US, which the tree does not override. So no timeout meets both while the firmware erases flash in the loop and the console write is uncapped. A window opens once the store moves to the FRAM (Q8) and the console write is capped below 500 ms less the rest of the pass and the reset; the cap is not stated. The image sets no timeout (V4). For the owner: the console-write cap and the timeout, in firmware. Not a defect of the part

report.value: pico-sdk 2.3.0 _watchdog_enable() sets every PSM_WDSEL bit except ROSC and XOSC (watchdog.c, the line after '// Reset everything apart from ROSC and XOSC'); WDSEL bit 4 is RESETS (Table 532), and the RESETS register resets with PADS_BANK0 (bit 9) and IO_BANK0 (bit 6) held in reset (Table 535). Section 9.7: 'resetting the PADS register block returns non-isolated pads to their reset state, but has no effect on isolated pads'; the ISO bits are not reset by that block reset. The SDK clears a pad's ISO bit in gpio_set_function(), so a pad in use returns to its reset state (section 9.3: output high-impedance through the null function, input disabled, pulled low). A pad left isolated keeps its latched state. Section 9.3's list of events that return the pads to their reset state names brownout, RUN low, SW-DP CDBGRSTREQ and RP-AP rescue reset, not the watchdog. The image enables no watchdog yet (V4). Not measured
